SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
D 3548.
Date 22/4/38

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, APRIL 17, 1938.

Shanghai Demilitarization
Plan Of S.M.C. Scored By
Chinese Ratepayers' Chief

Tao Lo-ching Replies To Statement Of Bell
That This Is China Territory And Recent
War Showed Too Few Troops Were Here

The declared determination of
Mr. A. D. Bell, new chairman of
the Shanghai Municipal Council, to
advocate the policy of demilitariza-
tion of the Shanghai area was
yesterday strongly criticized by Mr.
Tao Lo-ching, secretary general of
Chinese Ratepayers' Association,
who said in an interview with the
China Press that Mr. Bell had mis-
read the issue and effect of the
question.

He held the opinion that al-
though the Chinese government
and its citizens as one has the
right to protest such a policy be-
cause "Shanghai is obviously Chin-
ese territory."

"Unbiased" Belief

The spokesman for the Chinese
ratepayers expressed regret that
Mr. Bell should have made such a
statement without first consulting
the Chinese members of the Coun-
cil or the Chinese ratepayers them-
selves.

"Chinese citizens have the right
to protect their own homes and
property," he said. "If the Inter-
national Settlement is to be de-
militarized, then the Chinese gov-
ernment must be consulted. We
cannot accept any unilateral deci-
sion on this matter."

He pointed out that the presence
of foreign troops in Shanghai has
always been a source of friction
and misunderstanding. "The recent
war showed too few troops were
here to maintain order," he said.
"But that does not mean we should
accept demilitarization without
proper consultation."

Mr. Tao emphasized that the
Chinese ratepayers are willing to
cooperate with the Council in main-
taining peace and order, but they
must have a voice in decisions af-
fecting their safety and property.

"The presence of large numbers of
Chinese troops on the outskirts of
Shanghai might be a disturbing fac-
tor, but it has often been necessary
for the protection of Chinese citi-
zens and property. No foreign offi-
cial has the right to demand their
removal without proper consulta-
tion."

He recalled that when Mr. Bell
first appeared in Shanghai in 1932,
he had expressed similar views, but
later changed his opinion after see-
ing the situation firsthand. "We
hope Mr. Bell will do the same
this time," he said.

Mr. Tao concluded by saying that
the Chinese ratepayers would con-
tinue to press for their rights and
would not accept any decision made
without their consent.

（批：社 报
Passed Wym）

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与搜查登记处。
D 3548。
日期 1938年4月22日

《大美晚报》，1938年4月17日，星期日。

中国纳税人领袖抨击
工部局的上海非军事化计划

陶乐庆回应贝尔的声明，
称此乃中国领土，且近期战事
表明此地驻军过少

上海公共租界工部局新任主席
A. D. Bell 先生宣称决心倡导
上海地区非军事化政策，昨日遭
到华人纳税会秘书长陶乐庆先生
的强烈批评。陶先生在接受《大美
晚报》采访时称，贝尔先生误读
了该问题的实质及其影响。

他认为，尽管中国政府及其
公民作为一个整体有权抗议此类
政策，因为“上海显然是中国领
土”。

“公正”的信念

这位华人纳税人代表对贝尔
先生未先咨询工部局华董或华人
纳税人本身便发表此类言论表示
遗憾。

他说：“中国公民有权保护自
己的家园和财产。如果国际租界
要实行非军事化，则必须征询中
国政府的意见。我们不能接受在
此事上的任何单方面决定。”

他指出，外国军队在上海的
存在一直是摩擦和误解的根源。
他说：“近期的战争表明，此处
维持秩序的兵力太少。但这并不
意味着我们应在未经适当协商的
情况下接受非军事化。”

陶先生强调，华人纳税人愿
意与工部局合作以维持和平与秩
序，但在涉及其安全和财产的决
策中，他们必须拥有发言权。

“大量中国军队出现在上海郊
区可能是一个令人不安的因素，
但这往往对于保护中国公民和财
产是必要的。任何外国官员无权
在未经适当协商的情况下要求他
们撤离。”

他回顾说，当贝尔先生于
1932年初次来到上海时，曾表达
过类似观点，但在亲眼目睹局势
后改变了看法。“我们希望贝尔
先生这次也能如此，”他说。

陶先生最后表示，华人纳税人
将继续争取他们的权利，不会接
受任何未经他们同意而作出的决
定。

（批：社 报
Passed Wym）
